REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 28, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
SEPTEMBER 28, 2017, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by Recreation Division VolunTeens Eric Swint
  and Mina Hanna.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented to:

  SERVPRO (Business Spotlight).

  Andrea Gonzalez (Miss Guatemala US 2016).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Murali Vasudevan spoke regarding the Community Safety Committee, expressed
  concerns with increasing crime in the community, inquired about the status of the
  Cerritos Astor Museum, and the status of various Councilmember requests. He
  submitted a document for the record.

  Daisy Velasco expressed concerns regarding increasing crime in the community.

  Jay Gray requested expansion of the minutes, a list of businesses which are
  allowed to go door-to-door be provided to the Sheriff's Department, and
  conditions of approval for shopping centers for security, and directed Public Works
  to trim trees which are blocking the street lights.

  Darrell Engle inquired as to the link to the Library Committee on the City's
  website.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding the City's recent Community Safety
  Committee meeting where a presentation was made by Sheriff’s Captain Nunez.
  He requested the City televise the Community Safety Committee meetings, to
  communicate to residents that trees which are blocking street lights can have an
  expedited trimming schedule, and the benefits of LED lights for the streets.
 City of Cerritos  September 28, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sam Desai expressed concerns regarding the decision made by the City Council
  regarding the Temporary Use Permit at Cerritos College. He inquired as to the
  status of the City’s social media presence, the Cerritos Astor Museum, the need
  for a career/technical education center, and property lease revenues from the
  City’s property at Studebaker/Artesia.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of
  September 18, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes of September 18, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Registers of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 28,
  2017 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Registers of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  09/28/2017 $2,367,050.10 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Adoption of Ordinance – Introduced at the meeting of September 18, 2017.

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1016, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 3.20 OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH A DESIGN BUILD PROCUREMENT PROCESS FOR
  PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS IN FURTHERANCE OF ARTICLE IX OF THE CITY CHARTER
  (COUNCIL).

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF

9.  New and Old Business

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Solanki, and Yokoyama,
  Mayor Pro Tem Pulido, and Mayor Hu.

12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL—ANTICIPATED LITIGATION

  The City Council recessed into Closed Session to discuss the above referenced

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT: Mark Steres, City Attorney, reported the City
